items.source_name: Florida Governor's Office (Oct 13 Isaias recovery update, Jay/Vernon briefing)
items.summary: Florida Governor's Office (Tuesday Oct 13 update): power restored to 95% of customers in areas impacted by Hurricane Isaias, vs nearly 450,000 outages at the storm's height. FPL separately reported >380,000 outages restored (>85% of its affected customers) as of 10 p.m. CDT Monday, with restoration on track to be essentially complete in Escambia and Santa Rosa by end of Tuesday; PowerOutage.com showed >57,000 Florida customers still out as of Tuesday afternoon, mostly in those two counties. Edison Electric Institute: peak ~950,000 customers out across the region, >882,000 restored within 3 days. 11 Points of Distribution now operating across Escambia, Santa Rosa, Walton and Washington counties (water, meals, ice, tarps). Boil-water notices still in effect in 7 counties (Escambia, Holmes, Jackson, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Walton, Washington); ECUA expected to lift its precautionary notice Tuesday for mainland areas and Wednesday for Pensacola Beach.
items.title: Isaias recovery: 95% of impacted-area customers restored as of Tuesday, per governor's office; ~57,000 still out Tuesday afternoon

items.source_name: thefloridapress.com (updated Oct 13, 2026) / Florida Governor's Office press releases
items.summary: State recovery aid for the Isaias Panhandle (never previously in this feed): FloridaCommerce activated the $10M Florida Small Business Emergency Bridge Loan program (short-term zero-interest loans, applications through Nov 25, 2026 at FloridaJobs.org/DisasterRecovery/EBL); Agriculture Commissioner launched the Agriculture and Aquaculture Producers Natural Disaster Recovery Loan (interest-free, launched Oct 12); SNAP replacement benefits for storm food loss (request by Oct 19 at MyFLFamilies.com/Isaias); Insurance Assistance Hubs opened Oct 12 at UWF Pensacola (Parking Lot B, 11000 University Parkway) and Destin (Morgan Sports Complex, 4200 Indian Bayou Trail), 9 a.m.-4 p.m. Florida National Guard (~2,013 still activated Tuesday): 12,536 cubic acres of debris and 1,700 miles of roadway cleared, 17,441 cases of water + 8,387 MREs + 14,328 ice bags + 9,937 tarps distributed. All state-owned bridges inspected and reopened; 93% of traffic signals working; tolls suspended on Mid-Bay Bridge, Spence Parkway and Garcon Point Bridge. Curbside debris pickup starts Wednesday in Escambia and Santa Rosa (Santa Rosa estimates ~1.7M cubic yards of vegetative debris). Walmart committed $1M in funding and supplies.
items.title: Florida rolls out state recovery aid for Isaias Panhandle: $10M zero-interest business loans, farm loans, SNAP replacement, insurance hubs
